name: Chunghwa Telecom Co., Ltd.
moat_justification: Taiwan's incumbent and clear #1 operator: mobile revenue share 41.2% (record high, Q2 2026) above its 39.8% subscriber share, ~54.6% share of broadband access/internet, leading 5G share (~39%) and the incumbent fiber/last-mile network — scarce spectrum, sunk nationwide infrastructure and 0.36% postpaid churn support premium ARPU (5G migration fee uplift ~36%, postpaid ARPU +2.4% YoY, broadband ARPU rising). That is a real but narrow telecom moat, not a wide one: returns are capped by capital intensity and regulation, the market is saturated, and two capable rivals (Taiwan Mobile, Far EasTone) plus OTT erosion of legacy voice/SMS keep pricing power modest — hence 6/10, the top of moderate/narrow.

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x10.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Chunghwa Telecom Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-04-15), share capital note (Global depositary receipts) in the consolidated financial statements: one ADS represents 10 common stocks; the same statement appears in the company's Q1 2026 financial statements furnished on Form 6-K (filed 2026-05-11), and the Form F-6 registration describes each ADS as representing ten common shares) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
one_liner: Taiwan's dominant incumbent telecom, moat 6/10 — quality is not the issue, price is: Tier D, weighted IRR 6.8%, IV@15% $15.75 per ADS vs $46.51, and even the super-bull case ($26.59) sits far below the price; it clears 15% only under ~$15.75 per ADS.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: engine output predates release 5.5.0 — re-run the engine before an exit alert
moat_for: Taiwan's #1 operator: mobile revenue share 41.2% > subscriber share 39.8% (Q2 2026), ~54.6% of broadband access/internet, leading 5G share
Scarce licensed spectrum + sunk incumbent fiber/last-mile network rivals cannot replicate
Very low churn (postpaid 0.36%) and premium mix: 5G migration fee uplift ~36%, ARPU rising in mobile (+2.4% YoY) and broadband
Scale and enterprise/ICT bundling (cloud, cybersecurity, IDC, AIDC) anchored to the incumbent network and government/enterprise relationships
Fortress, defensive cash generation: net cash balance sheet, OE positive 5/5 years, minimal SBC
moat_against: Saturated, mature Taiwan market: core growth is low-single-digit; smartphone penetration already >90%
Capital-intensive and regulated: spectrum/network capex never stops and the NCC caps the return the moat can earn
Two capable, consolidated rivals (Taiwan Mobile, Far EasTone) contest every segment; entry-tier price competition persists
OTT erosion of legacy fixed voice/SMS; the fast-growing ICT revenue is project-based, lumpy and lower-margin than core telecom
State influence (Ministry of Transportation and Communications is the largest shareholder) and TWD/USD exposure for ADS holders
